The displayed bounds are wrong in both cases (e.g. R=1,d=2: F²=1.5>log 2 for m+ν=0; n=3,m=1,R=1,d=2: F²=1/2>1/3=R^{2ν}/(2(m+ν))). The G case display corresponds to the integrand r^{-2m-2ν+3} instead of the correct (m+2ν)²R^{2m+4ν}r^{-2m-2ν-1}, is false in some regimes, and its cases m+ν∈{0,1,2} never apply for odd n (half-integral m+ν). H² uses m² instead of the Laplace–Beltrami eigenvalue λ_m=m(m+2ν) from (defiotamnumber), so the quantity defined in (wfourier) is not the H¹ norm for n≥3. Since the factor (m+2ν) vanishes for the constant mode (m,ν)=(0,0) (present for n=2, with F²=(d²−R²)/2>0), the culminating max-bound and the final continuity estimate ‖u‖_{H¹}≤C(Σ(m+2ν)|ĝ|²)^{1/2} are false for constant Dirichlet data in n=2 (positive left side, zero right side).

issues.failure_explanation: (eqn:C_F) is claimed with the H^{-1/2}(S_R)-norm of ∂_r v, but the proof's contradiction hypothesis assumes ‖∂_r v_k‖_{L²(S_R)}→0, a strictly stronger condition (not even defined for a general normal derivative in H^{-1/2}(S_R)); a sequence violating (eqn:C_F) need only satisfy ‖∂_r v_k‖_{H^{-1/2}}→0. Hence the argument establishes at best the weaker L²-based inequality. In addition, the ambient space H¹(Ω,S_R) is ill-defined as written (γ₁ is defined only on H¹(ω,Δ), and the 'natural norm' takes the L²(Γ)-norm of an H^{-1/2}-valued trace), and the asserted completeness of H=∪_z ker(γ₁−DtN(z)γ₀) does not follow from continuity of DtN(s). The stated inequality is nevertheless true: a corrected proof uses weak H¹(Ω)-convergence, the compact trace H¹(Ω)→L²(S_R), and the definiteness estimate thm:DtN(iii), (n−2)/2‖g_k‖²_{L²(S_R)}≤‖∂_r v_k‖_{H^{-1/2}}‖g_k‖_{H^{1/2}}, to get g_k→0 in L²(S_R), forcing the constant weak limit to vanish.

They neither ensure S_R⊂∂Ω — which the proof needs in order to apply thm:C_Friedrich on Ω (applied on ω it yields only ‖v‖_{L²(ω)} and ω-norms, so the Ω-norms in (vL2esta) do not follow) and to use the boundary trace estimate with C_{Ω,0} for (esttr) — nor that ω is adjacent to S_R so that the normal derivative in (normaltraceest) coincides with ∂_r v. issues.failure_explanation: With the normalizations (deffm12) and K_μ(z)∼√(π/2z)e^{−z}, I_μ(z)∼e^z/√(2πz), the true leading behaviour is f^{(1)}(z)∼(π/2)e^{−z}z^{−ν−1/2} and f^{(2)}(z)∼(2π)^{−1}e^{z}z^{−ν−1/2}, so the displayed relations with leading constant 1 are false already on the positive real axis (m=0, ν=1/2: f^{(1)}(z)=(π/2)e^{−z}/z, f^{(2)}(z)=sinh(z)/(πz)). Moreover the e^{z}-expansion of I_μ holds only for |arg z|<π/2: on the imaginary axis f^{(2)}(iy)(iy)^{ν+1/2}e^{−iy} oscillates (for m=0, ν=1/2 it equals (1−e^{−2iy})/(2π)) instead of converging. Consequently the derivation of (fundsrad) and of the mode selection 'IC^Green ⟺ B_{m,j,ν}=0' — which underlies (specsolrep), (eqn:DtN_def), (GreenStrong), and hence PropProblems.1b and the proof of thm:DtN — is unsupported as written; in particular, for purely imaginary s the resulting O(e^{sr})=O(1) bound cannot exclude the I-modes. All these conclusions are true (the I-mode combination has a non-vanishing oscillatory leading term), but they require a separate argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State (fundsysasy) with the correct leading constants (π/2 and 1/(2π)) and restrict it to |arg z|≤π/2−δ; exclude the I-modes on the imaginary axis by a separate argument (e.g. via I_μ(−ikr)∝J_μ(kr) as in Step 2 of the proof of thm:zmn, or a Rellich-type argument).
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the spectral representation of the solution and DtN operators and of the implication (GreenStrong) used for PropProblems.1b is invalid as written, especially for purely imaginary wavenumbers; the representations themselves and all resulting theorems are true and recoverable by standard arguments.
